newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-CLOSE WINS FOR PINTO AND CHEPCHUMBA IN LONDON MARATHON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CLOSE WINS FOR PINTO AND CHEPCHUMBA IN LONDON MARATHON.

text.p: Portugal's Antonio Pinto ran the year's best time on Sunday to snatch victory in the London marathon in one of the closest finishes in the history of the event.
Pinto repeated his 1992 victory in London by winning the men's race in two hours seven minutes 55 seconds, the fastest time of the year in a marathon.

Italy's Stefano Baldini was second in 2:07.57 with the two-second gap being the smallest in the race's 17-year history, apart from the inaugural race when the two front runners deliberately staged a dead heat.
The race had looked set to be decided between Baldini and South Africa's Josiah Thugwane, the 1996 Olympic champion, who broke away after 22 miles (35 kms).
But Pinto, who had been part of the leading group until the pair made their effort, clawed back the deficit.
As Thugwane began to flag, Pinto drew level with Baldini on the approach to the finish and then sprinted for the line.
The women's race was also decided on a sprint finish with Kenya's Joyce Chepchumba just beating Briton Liz McColgan, reversing their 1996 placings.
Germany's Sonja Krojik, who was eventually to finish fourth, made an audacious bid for victory from the halfway mark and at one stage was 50 seconds clear of the chasing pack.
But defending champion McColgan and Chepchumba swept past Krojik with just over two miles (three kms) to go.
McColgan looked set to retain her title as she held a narrow lead around the final turn in St James's Park but the Kenyan dug deep to pass her at the finish.
Chepchumba won in 2:26:51 seconds with McColgan just one second further back. Romania's Lidia Simon finished third in 2:27:11.
More than 29,000 runners started the marathon, the biggest ever field in the race.
